text:
sam: Heads-up — onboarding 13B-q8 run shows consistent quality regression vs fp16 when sliding_window=true and rope_scaling!=1.0. failing evals on summarization set, odd token-level shifts in outputs.
anya: ugh. which config fields are different from our default? can you paste the config.json used in conversion? :eyes:
sam: sure. relevant bits:
```json
{"architectures": ["SomeModel"], "max_position_embeddings": 2048, "rope_scaling": {"type": "dynamic", "factor": 0.75}, "sliding_window": true, "num_key_value_heads": 32}
```
mj: quick note: the hf checkpoint had num_key_value_heads=16 originally? if we doubled heads during conversion that's a red flag.
lena: I ran a smoke decode and saw KV cache indexing errors in logs:
```
WARNING kv_lookup: idx=2048 out_of_range -> wrapping to 0
```
that looks like off-by-one / maxpos mismatch when sliding window shifts tokens in the cache.
sam: exactly. quantized binary shows different branch due to kernel layout changes; rope_scaling modifies the rotary position indices and with sliding_window we shift positions, so combined with wrong num_kv_heads the KV layout misaligns.
oliver: can you repro deterministically? share the minimal prompt + seed.
sam: repro script:
```
python repro.py --model converted-13b-q8 --prompt "Summarize: <long text>" --seed 42 --max_new_tokens 256
```
I attached diff of fp16 vs q8 tokens — shift starts at token 37.
eval-bot: eval/summary_regression | model: converted-13b-q8 | dataset: summa-100 | rouge-l drop: 6.2 | p-value: 0.0012
anya: 6.2 rouge-l is large. Is the conversion step mapping hf.rope_scale -> rope_scaling correctly? maybe HF uses "rope_scaling": {"type":"linear", "factor":...} vs our expected shape.
mj: also check chat template token boundaries — sliding_window true means we keep a running context; if max_position_embeddings is 2048 but the tokenizer uses special chat tokens with added length, effective positions exceed maxpos and wrap.
lena: checked the original HF config.json: it had "num_key_value_heads": 16 and "max_position_embeddings": 4096. we truncated to 2048 accidentally during a size-normalization in conversion.
sam: that explains the wrap. when sliding_window=true we rely on >prompt_len maxpos to avoid wrap, but truncation causes idx to overflow and rope scaling multiplies indices causing misaligned rotaries.
chris: action: 1) revert max_position_embeddings to 4096 in converted config and rerun smoke. 2) ensure num_key_value_heads preserved (16). 3) add unit test in conversion that compares hf_config.json -> redwood_config.json for these four keys.
oliver: I started a quick patch to conversion tool, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/convert-tool/pull/452
anja: mj, can you run quantized smoke after revert? tag me when results ready.
mj: running now on a single V100 (q8 run)
(eval-bot posts automated logs)
eval-bot: convert-check | mismatch: num_key_value_heads (hf=16 -> redwood=32) -> FAIL
eval-bot: post-fix-smoke | started job id r-20277 at 2775012380
mj: quick results: rouge-l drop down to 0.4 after restoring maxpos and kv heads. still tiny differences due to quant noise but within threshold.
lena: added conversion unit test:
```
assert converted['num_key_value_heads'] == hf_original['num_key_value_heads']
assert converted['max_position_embeddings'] >= hf_original['max_position_embeddings']
```
chris: nice. also add explicit handling for rope_scaling variants: normalize types ("dynamic" vs "linear") and ensure factor semantics match HF.
sam: logging note: when sliding_window=true we should log effective_position = token_pos + sliding_offset and assert effective_position < max_position_embeddings at runtime to avoid silent wraps.
anya: agree. also write a short doc blurb in onboarding checklist: "verify kv heads, maxpos, rope_scaling types, sliding_window semantics".
oliver: I'll merge the conversion patch and the unit test, then trigger a full quantized CI run.
chris: timeline: merge today, CI run overnight, should have green by tomorrow morning. thanks team :tada:
sam: thanks all — saved a weird regression. will follow up with postmortem if anything else crops up.
